section_summary: This section documents the political crises, cabinet reorganizations, and administrative restructuring in Japan from late August 1939 to mid-January 1940. Following the announcement of the German-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact, Prime Minister Kiichiro Hiranuma's cabinet resigned to assume responsibility, leading to the formation of a government under General Nobuyuki Abe with military leadership dominating key posts and attempts to reorient foreign policy. Facing mounting popular and parliamentary discontent over price inflation, commodity shortages, and ineffective economic controls—culminating in a Diet resolution signed by 250 members demanding his resignation—Premier Abe resigned in January 1940, leading to deliberations that culminated in the formation of the Yonai Cabinet.

subfiles.about: Report extract discussing the expansion of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the creation of the Price Bureau, and the consolidation of wartime economic controls under the General Mobilization Act.
subfiles.summary: This concluding page of an embassy report details the expansion of ten existing bureaus within the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and the establishment of two new bodies: the Price Bureau and the Deliberative Council for the Adjustment of Demand and Supply of Commodities. The General Affairs Bureau is charged with industrial development and material mobilization across Japan, Manchukuo, and China, while the Price Bureau is empowered under Article 19 of the General Mobilization Act to regulate commodity prices. These administrative adjustments aim to consolidate emergency economic controls established since the outbreak of the China Incident.
subfiles.title: Report on the Reorganization of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and Economic Control Measures

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 388 regarding a review by the Japanese inner Cabinet of relations with Germany and Italy.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State cross-reference sheet indexing telegram No. 388 of August 4, 1939, from Chargé d'Affaires Eugene H. Dooman in Tokyo. The underlying telegram reports that the Japanese inner Cabinet intended to conduct a general review of the international situation, with particular focus on relations with Germany and Italy. The original telegram was filed under decimal file 762.94/397.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Review of International Situation by Japanese Inner Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 390 reporting that General Sadao Araki would likely become Prime Minister if the government falls.
subfiles.summary: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing telegram No. 390 of August 5, 1939, sent from Tokyo by Eugene H. Dooman. It records information received indicating that in the event of the Japanese Government's collapse, General Sadao Araki would be designated as the next Prime Minister. The original document was placed in decimal file 762.94/400.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: General Sadao Araki as Prospective Prime Minister

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 394 concerning the precarious standing and probable fall of the Japanese Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet referencing Tokyo telegram No. 394 of August 8, 1939, from Eugene H. Dooman. The document notes that the Japanese Cabinet was occupying an increasingly weak political position, leading many observers to anticipate its imminent fall. The original telegram was filed under decimal file 762.94/402.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Weak Position and Anticipated Fall of the Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Rush telegram reporting the resignation of the Japanese Cabinet and the imperial command to General Nobuyuki Abe to form a new government.
subfiles.summary: A rush telegram sent from Tokyo on August 28, 1939, by Chargé d'Affaires Eugene H. Dooman to the Secretary of State. Dooman reports that the entire Japanese Cabinet resigned that morning. He further advises that General Nobuyuki Abe has been called upon to form a new Cabinet.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 442 from Tokyo: Resignation of Cabinet and Selection of General Abe

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting Japanese press speculation regarding potential appointees to key ministerial portfolios in the incoming Abe Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A two-page telegram sent by Eugene H. Dooman from Tokyo on August 28, 1939, relaying Japanese press reports on ministerial candidates for General Abe's cabinet. Proposed candidates include Lieutenant General Rensuke Isogai for War, Vice Admiral Zengo Yoshida for Navy, Ambassador Mamoru Shigemitsu for Foreign Affairs, and Juichi Tsushima, Kazue Shoda, or Kazuo Aoki for Finance. Additionally, Minseito party leader Ryutaro Nagai is expected to join the cabinet as Minister of Railways or Communications.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 443 from Tokyo: Press Speculation on Ministerial Candidates for the Abe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 440 regarding the Japanese Cabinet's approval of the Prime Minister's resignation over the Soviet-German pact.
subfiles.summary: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing telegram No. 440 of August 26, 1939, from Eugene H. Dooman in Tokyo. It records that the Japanese Cabinet approved Prime Minister Hiranuma's decision to tender his resignation. The political change was prompted by the Prime Minister's desire to assume responsibility for the Japanese Government's failure to anticipate the conclusion of the Soviet-German Non-Aggression Pact.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Cabinet Resignation Following the Soviet-German Pact

subfiles.about: Strictly confidential telegram reporting that the Foreign Affairs portfolio has been offered to retired Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura.
subfiles.summary: A strictly confidential telegram sent by Eugene H. Dooman from Tokyo on September 19, 1939. Dooman reports that the post of Minister for Foreign Affairs has been offered to Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura. The telegram highlights Nomura's past service as naval attaché in Washington in 1921 and commander of Japanese naval forces in Shanghai in 1932.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 485 from Tokyo: Foreign Affairs Portfolio Offered to Admiral Nomura

subfiles.about: Confidential telegram confirming the formal appointment of Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura as Minister of Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.summary: A confidential telegram sent by Eugene H. Dooman from Tokyo on September 25, 1939, to the Secretary of State. Dooman confirms that Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura was formally appointed Minister of Foreign Affairs that afternoon. The message was also repeated to American diplomatic missions in Shanghai, Peiping, and Chungking.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 490 from Tokyo: Formal Appointment of Admiral Nomura as Foreign Minister

subfiles.about: State Department Immigration Section search slips listing previous decimal file numbers indexed under Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura.
subfiles.from: Division of Communication and Records, Immigration Section
subfiles.summary: Two index search sheets completed on September 22, 1939, by the Immigration Section of the Division of Communication and Records. The slips list State Department decimal file numbers relating to Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura, spanning from 1920 to 1939. The search compiled departmental files concerning Nomura's previous diplomatic and naval visits following his appointment as Foreign Minister.
subfiles.title: General Card Index Search Slips on Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting Japanese press acclaim for Nomura's appointment and speculation on diplomatic reassignments, including Yosuke Matsuoka.
subfiles.summary: A two-page telegram sent by Eugene H. Dooman from Tokyo on September 26, 1939. It notes unanimous Japanese press praise for Admiral Nomura's appointment as Foreign Minister, interpreting it as an initiative to improve Japanese-American relations. The dispatch also forecasts major changes in Japanese diplomatic missions abroad, noting that Ambassador Kensuke Horinouchi in Washington is expected to be replaced, with former South Manchuria Railway president Yosuke Matsuoka widely mentioned as a successor.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 491 from Tokyo: Press Reaction to Nomura's Appointment and Expected Diplomatic Shifts

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 446 on the resignation of the Hiranuma Cabinet and transition to a new foreign policy.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet indexing telegram No. 446 of August 29, 1939, from Eugene H. Dooman in Tokyo. The underlying report discusses the ongoing change of government following the resignation of the Hiranuma Cabinet. It highlights favorable press reaction to Baron Hiranuma's explanation that the resignation emphasized cabinet responsibility for the German-Soviet Treaty and symbolized the adoption of a new foreign policy.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Resignation of Hiranuma Cabinet and Adoption of New Foreign Policy

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 448 on the formal appointment of the Abe Cabinet and press descriptions of it as nonentities.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet referencing telegram No. 448 of August 30, 1939, from Eugene H. Dooman in Tokyo. It notes the formal appointment of cabinet ministers under General Nobuyuki Abe and highlights critical press commentary describing the cabinet as a collection of nonentities. The note also records the press view that the cabinet's primary justification for existence is formulating an independent foreign policy free from European entanglements.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Formation and Press Criticism of the Abe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 447 setting forth the press announcement of the composition of the Abe Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet referencing telegram No. 447 of August 30, 1939, from Eugene H. Dooman in Tokyo. It indexes the press announcement setting forth the ministerial roster of the new cabinet under General Nobuyuki Abe as successor to Hiranuma. The referenced communication was filed under decimal file 894.00/867.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Make-up of New Cabinet under General Nobuyuki Abe

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting the press announcement of the full ministerial lineup of the newly formed Cabinet of General Nobuyuki Abe.
subfiles.summary: A two-page telegram sent by Eugene H. Dooman from Tokyo on August 30, 1939, reporting the ministerial lineup of the Abe Cabinet as announced by the press. The roster lists Prime Minister General Nobuyuki Abe concurrently holding Foreign Affairs, General Shunroku Hata as War Minister, Vice Admiral Zengo Yoshida as Navy Minister, and Naoshi Ohara holding Home Affairs and Social Welfare. Other appointments include Kazuo Aoki (Finance and Cabinet Planning Board), Takao Godo (Commerce and Industry, Agriculture), Ryutaro Nagai (Communications, Railways), Kakichi Kawarada (Education), Tsuneo Kanemitsu (Overseas Affairs), and Ryusaku Endo (Chief Cabinet Secretary).
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 447 from Tokyo: Official Lineup of the New Abe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 504 on Foreign Office opposition to curtailment of its functions and cabinet dissension.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet indexing telegram No. 504 of October 5, 1939, from Eugene H. Dooman in Tokyo. It reports on internal dissension within the Abe Cabinet caused by Foreign Office resistance to proposals transferring its commercial functions to a new Trade Ministry. The document notes that bureaucratic conflict has sparked growing skepticism regarding the durability of the cabinet.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Foreign Office Protests and Cabinet Dissension over Trade Ministry

subfiles.about: Memorandum analyzing Nomura's prospective appointment as evidence of the complete militarization and military coordination of the Japanese state.
subfiles.summary: A memorandum from Adviser on Political Relations Stanley K. Hornbeck to Secretary of State Cordell Hull, dated September 19/20, 1939. Hornbeck argues that the appointment of Admiral Nomura as Foreign Minister further illustrates how Japan has unified policy and execution under military control. With military officers heading the premiership, War, Navy, and Foreign Office, Hornbeck observes that Japan operates as a militarized machine capable of pursuing national objectives through armed force.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Stanley K. Hornbeck on Militarization of the Japanese Government

subfiles.about: Biographical memorandum prepared for the Secretary of State summarizing Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura's diplomatic and naval record.
subfiles.summary: A memorandum prepared by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs for Secretary of State Cordell Hull on September 19, 1939, providing biographical information on Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura. It summarizes his service in Austria and Germany, participation in the Versailles Peace Conference and the Washington Naval Conference, and his tenure as Naval Attaché in Washington. It also notes his command during the 1932 Shanghai hostilities, where he lost an eye in a bomb attack, and describes him as an able statesman favorably disposed toward the United States.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs: Biographic Data on Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura

subfiles.about: Memorandum commenting on Hugh Byas's press analysis of Premier Abe, Admiral Yoshida's 1936 visit to the U.S., and General Hata.
subfiles.summary: A memorandum written by Stanley K. Hornbeck to Secretary Hull and Under Secretary Welles on September 2, 1939. Hornbeck praises Hugh Byas's commentary in the New York Times on Premier Abe and reviews the background of Navy Minister Admiral Zengo Yoshida, recalling his 1936 training ship visit to American ports. He notes a report from the Naval Attaché in Peiping stating Yoshida was responsible for Japan's U.S. war plan, and compares published photographs of Yoshida and War Minister General Shunroku Hata.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Stanley K. Hornbeck on Premier Abe, Admiral Yoshida, and General Hata
subfiles.to: Secretary of State and Under Secretary Sumner Welles

subfiles.about: New York Times article on the formation of the Abe Cabinet, key military leaders, border hostilities, and diplomatic reorientation.
subfiles.summary: A two-page clipping from The New York Times of August 30, 1939, featuring reports by Hugh Byas from Tokyo and wireless dispatches from Chungking. It reports the formation of General Nobuyuki Abe's cabinet, emphasizing the appointments of China war veterans General Shunroku Hata and Admiral Zengo Yoshida, alongside portraits of both ministers. The analysis discusses Abe's compromising reputation, reductions in cabinet portfolios, fighting along the Khalka River on the Manchukuo-Outer Mongolia border, and speculation that Japan may seek rapprochement with Great Britain.
subfiles.title: Newspaper Clipping: 'New Cabinet in Japan Announced by Abe' by Hugh Byas (The New York Times)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing despatch 4139 transmitting the Abe Cabinet's platform as published in the Japan Advertiser.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet referencing despatch No. 4139 of September 20, 1939, from Eugene H. Dooman in Tokyo. It indexes a report and attached newspaper clipping from the Japan Advertiser of September 14 outlining the newly adopted policy platform of the Abe Cabinet. The original despatch was filed under decimal file 894.00/878.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Platform of the Abe Cabinet Reported in the Japan Advertiser

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing despatch 4175 regarding Foreign Office resistance against the creation of a Trade Ministry.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet indexing despatch No. 4175 of October 10, 1939, from Eugene H. Dooman in Tokyo. The underlying report details developments and political speculation surrounding intense opposition within the Foreign Office to the creation of a separate Trade Ministry. The original document was placed in decimal file 894.00/880.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Foreign Office Opposition to Projected Trade Ministry

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing despatch 4181 containing an embassy report on the platform of the Abe Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet referencing despatch No. 4181 of October 16, 1939, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. It notes the receipt of a periodic political report concerning the platform and policy program announced by the Abe Cabinet. The original paper was filed under decimal file 894.00 P.R./142.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Periodic Report on the Platform of the Abe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Embassy report section analyzing the five-point platform announced by the Abe Cabinet on September 13, 1939.
subfiles.summary: An extract from American Embassy Tokyo Despatch No. 4181 (Periodic Report No. 142) reviewing the platform issued by the Abe Cabinet on September 13, 1939. The platform stressed settlement of the China Incident, positive assistance in creating a new regime in China, industrial expansion across Japan, Manchukuo, and China, foreign trade adjustments, national mobilization (including price controls and labor mobilization), and internal administrative reform. The report remarks that the platform offered little new policy substance and met with public apathy.
subfiles.title: Report Extract on the Platform of the Abe Cabinet (Despatch No. 4181)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 713 regarding a resolution signed by 250 Diet members urging Prime Minister Abe to resign.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet indexing telegram No. 713 of December 28, 1939, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. It reports on a resolution signed by 250 members of the Diet requesting the resignation of Prime Minister Abe, reflecting growing popular discontent against expanding state economic controls. The note also discusses the timing of a possible cabinet collapse and required leadership qualities for a successor. The original telegram was filed under decimal file 894.00/884.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Diet Resolution Calling for Resignation of Prime Minister Abe

subfiles.about: Detailed telegram analyzing the Diet resolution demanding Abe's resignation, widespread public unrest over inflation, and prospective successors.
subfiles.summary: A four-page telegram sent in two sections by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew from Tokyo on December 28, 1939. Grew reports that 250 Diet members submitted a resolution urging Prime Minister Abe to resign, reflecting widespread public revolt against soaring commodity prices, ineffective anti-inflation measures, and burdensome wartime economic controls. Cabinet councilors and political insiders unanimously consider the cabinet's tenure doomed, debating whether resignation will occur during the New Year recess or at the close of the Diet session in March. Grew observes that while supporters of Admiral Mineo Osumi and General Kazushige Ugaki are active, the public seeks a leader capable of uniting political factions and executing drastic measures to resolve internal and external crises.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 713 (Sections 1 and 2) from Tokyo: Political Crisis and Diet Revolt Against the Abe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 18 on the resignation of Prime Minister Abe and negotiations to select a successor.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet indexing telegram No. 18 of January 14, 1940, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. It records reports that Prime Minister Nobuyuki Abe tendered the resignation of his cabinet to the Emperor and outlines subsequent consultations to choose a new premier. The original telegram was filed under decimal file 894.00/890.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Resignation of Premier Abe and Search for a Successor

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting that Premier Abe has resigned and describing political obstacles in choosing a new Prime Minister.
subfiles.summary: A two-page telegram sent by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew from Tokyo on January 14, 1940. Grew reports that Premier Nobuyuki Abe formally submitted his resignation to the Emperor, who accepted it and instructed Lord Keeper of the Privy Seal Kurahei Yuasa to recommend a new premier. The dispatch notes that consultations with the Genro (Prince Saionji) and formal political maneuvers are underway, while Prince Fumimaro Konoe firmly refuses to reassume the premiership. Grew highlights that the army's reluctance to assume direct political responsibility and Konoe's refusal complicate the selection of a candidate able to form a strong cabinet.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 18 from Tokyo: Resignation of Premier Abe and Deliberations on Successor Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 23 regarding fixed appointments for Foreign Affairs, Navy, and War in the new cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet referencing telegram No. 23 of January 15, 1940, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. It lists ministerial posts definitely fixed in the incoming cabinet, reporting that Hachiro Arita will serve as Foreign Minister, Admiral Zengo Yoshida will remain as Navy Minister, and General Shunroku Hata will continue as Minister of War. The original document was placed in decimal file 894.00/892.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Key Ministerial Appointments in the Incoming Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing telegram 25 confirming that all positions in the new Cabinet have been filled.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet indexing telegram No. 25 of January 16, 1940, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. It confirms that all ministerial portfolios in the new Japanese Cabinet have been finalized and provides the full roster of ministers. The referenced telegram was filed under decimal file 894.00/895.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Completion of All Appointments in the New Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing despatch 4377 reporting on the appointment of new ministers in the Japanese Cabinet during November 1939.
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet referencing despatch No. 4377 of December 28, 1939, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. It indexes a monthly political report for November 1939 detailing the appointment of full-time ministers for Welfare and Railways in the Abe Cabinet. The original despatch was filed under decimal file 894.00 P.R./144.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Report on New Ministerial Appointments for November 1939

subfiles.about: Comprehensive political report reviewing cabinet expansion, party overtures, administrative paralysis, price control revisions, and military armaments policy.
subfiles.summary: A five-page extract from American Embassy Tokyo Despatch No. 4377 (Periodic Report No. 144 for November 1939) reviewing internal Japanese political conditions. It details the appointments of Kiyoshi Akita (Welfare) and Hidejiro Nagata (Railways), marking the formal abandonment of Abe's small-cabinet concept, alongside Minseito leader Chuji Machida's refusal to accept a portfolio. The report examines entrenched bureaucratic opposition that stalled the proposed Trade Ministry and civil service tenure reform, reviews Commerce Minister Godo's adoption of 'appropriate prices' amidst severe commodity inflation and market hoarding, and analyzes public statements by Premier Abe and War Minister Shunroku Hata stressing army replenishment and continental defense against potential rivals.
subfiles.title: Report Extract on Internal Political Conditions in Japan (Despatch No. 4377 / Periodic Report No. 144)
